inventory.source: Bangladesh brick kilns from space (Sentinel-2 detector trained on SentinelKilnDB), dry season 2024-25
inventory.precision: Its audit finds about 8 in 10 detections inside SentinelKilnDB's labelled footprints are kilns and about 2 in 10 outside; 'labelled' here means the detection sits on a human-labelled kiln.
inventory.not_seen: A cold kiln and a working kiln look alike from above, so these are kiln structures, not kilns in operation.

firms.note: Random places are at least 1 km from every mapped kiln. VIIRS 'low' confidence detections are excluded in the not-low figure, as in the record.

static_sources.note: FIRMS persistent heat sources (type 1-3, 0.01 degree cells) against every inventory detection.

night_lights.note: Cells brighter than 15 nW/cm2/sr in the monsoon are left out: city lights drown a kiln's. If kilns had no effect, 25% would be above the random 75th percentile. Kilns cluster on the edges of towns, which also brighten in the dry season, and random places include empty land, so this is consistent with kilns, not proof of them.

radar.contrast: VV within 100 m minus VV in a 300-800 m ring, seasonal medians
radar.note: If kilns did not differ from random places, 25% would be above the random 75th percentile. A bright dry-season contrast shows a built structure stands out from its surroundings; the rise since the monsoon is the part that brick stacks would add. Radar also responds to buildings, embankments and moisture, so this is consistent with kilns, not proof of them, and it says nothing about whether a kiln is firing.

caveat: Kiln evidence comes from outside FIRMS. FIRMS is shown only to measure how little of the kiln belt it sees.
